name: qloop
tagline: Hand a goal to a real agentic loop, and be able to prove what it did.
description: QLoop gives an Objective to a model's own native loop (claude -p or codex exec) on a governed fleet dev server, turn by turn, and witnesses every turn on a tamper-evident hash chain. The loop can only touch the tools you named, live gates pause it on budget or interval, and a human halt fires a signed kill that actually ends the process. When it finishes you can replay what it believed at any moment, with the causal chain of envelopes behind each step.
shortDescription: The governed agentic loop that proves itself
author: QUOX
_pricingNote: PROVISIONAL. DEVSUITE plan keeps bundle SKU + final pricing owner-gated; this figure exists so the manifest is well-formed and the plugin can be enabled, not as an approved price.
dashboardSurfaceNote: No dedicated route by design: QLoop is an execution mode of /objectives, a core surface. Gating that whole route on this plugin would break core objectives for orgs that do not hold it.
dataPlaneNote: Objectives are served by the TASKS service at /api/objectives (authenticated + rate limited), not through the collector /api/v1 proxy the other members use. This is an architectural difference, not a missing route: QLoop is an execution mode of the core objectives engine rather than a standalone plugin backend.
corePositioningNote: Moved OUT of the Dev Suite bundle and INTO core, 2026-08-19 (owner decision). QLoop is not a development tool: anything can drive a loop — working an inbox, watching a queue, chasing a reconciliation. It is the DAG objectives engine grown up, which is core machinery. Hermes and OpenClaw give their loop away, so a price ticket on ours invites exactly the wrong comparison. NOTE: launching a loop still defaults to the FLEET spawner (services/tasks/lib/loopDispatch.js defaultLoopSpawner = createFleetLoopSpawner), so a core-local spawner is the outstanding work before this claim is fully true. The seam is already injectable.
marketingPoints: A real agentic loop, not a pre-decomposed task list: the model gets the goal and the tools and runs its own loop
Every turn witnessed on a tamper-evident chain, so tampering with a stored turn breaks verification
Deny-by-default tool scope: reaching outside it is interrupted and written down
A human halt with teeth, proven on real hardware: the process ends, the turns freeze, the reason is witnessed
Replay a finished loop and see what it believed at any point in time
Runs on both Claude and Codex through one seam

witnessedTurns.name: Every turn witnessed
witnessedTurns.description: Each turn is hashed into a WARD chain as it happens, carrying its sequence and a content hash. A 19-turn run landed all 19 on an intact chain, each entry recomputed and linked to its predecessor.

scopedTools.name: Deny-by-default scope
scopedTools.description: The loop can only use the tools you named. Where a backend cannot honour a pattern the scope fails loud instead of silently widening.

liveGates.name: Gates while it runs
liveGates.description: Budget thresholds, interval check-ins and denials fire during the run, not only before it. A deny fires the same signed kill as a halt.

evidenceReplay.name: Replay the evidence
evidenceReplay.description: Scrub through a finished loop's envelope chain and reconstruct what it believed at any moment, with the causal chain behind each step.
